cleanIntro: The RF-22LR comes apart the way a 10/22-pattern rifle does — one takedown screw, the barreled receiver out of the stock, then the trigger group and the bolt out of the receiver. Radical's book makes one point about why it matters: the RF-22LR is built to tighter tolerances than the pattern it follows, and rimfire ammunition is dirty, so it wants cleaning and lubrication after every use rather than when it starts to complain.

steps.title: Magazine out, bolt open, look — then look again
steps.action: Point the rifle somewhere safe, take the magazine out, and pull the bolt open. Then look into the chamber and see it empty, and do it a second time. Radical prints this warning at the head of the disassembly, and a rimfire is the rifle where a round left in the chamber is easiest to miss.
steps.quote: Point the rifle in a safe direction, remove the magazine, open the bolt and visually check that the rifle is unloaded. Then check it again.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL RF-22LR — Radical Firearms — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — RF22LR Enhanced Bolt, Disassembly from the Receiver, p.7
steps.warn: NEVER ASSUME A FIREARM IS COMPLETELY UNLOADED AND IS SAFE. THIS IS ESPECIALLY TRUE OF RIMFIRE RIFLES.

steps.title: Barrel band screw out — if your stock has one
steps.action: If the rifle wears a barrel band, take its screw out first so the barrel is free of the stock at the front. Many stocks have no band at all, and the book says so: this step is only for rifles that carry one.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel band (if attached) screw.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL RF-22LR — Radical Firearms — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Disassembly from the Receiver, step 2, p.7

steps.title: Takedown screw out
steps.action: Remove the takedown screw under the stock, ahead of the magazine well. It is the one screw that holds the barreled receiver in the stock; keep it somewhere it will not roll away.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL RF-22LR — Radical Firearms — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Disassembly from the Receiver, step 3, p.7

steps.title: Cross-bolt safety to the MIDDLE, then lift the action out
steps.action: Push the cross-bolt safety to a middle position — neither fully on nor fully off — and lift the barreled receiver up out of the stock. Radical gives the reason in its own words: left fully on or fully off, the safety can damage the stock as the action comes out.
steps.quote: Set the cross bolt safety in a middle position. This prevents damage to the stock assembly. Lift the barreled receiver assembly from the stock.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL RF-22LR — Radical Firearms — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Disassembly from the Receiver, step 4, p.7

steps.title: Trigger group pins out, safety to ON
steps.action: Drift the two side pins out of the receiver to free the trigger assembly, then lift the trigger group away and push its safety to ON. Use a punch to drift them, and keep them together with the group so they go back where they came from.
steps.quote: Drift out the two side pins holding the trigger assembly and push the safety to ON.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL RF-22LR — Radical Firearms — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Disassembly from the Receiver, step 5, p.7

steps.title: Receiver upside down, buffer pin out
steps.action: Turn the receiver upside down and remove the buffer pin at the rear. That pin is the bolt's rear stop; with it out, the bolt has room to come back far enough to lift free.
steps.quote: Remove the buffer pin at the rear of the receiver.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL RF-22LR — Radical Firearms — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Disassembly from the Receiver, steps 6–7, p.7

steps.title: Bolt fully back, lift the front, let the handle go
steps.action: Push the bolt all the way to the rear and, while holding it there, lift its front end and release the bolt handle. The two movements happen together — back and up — and that is what separates the bolt from its handle.
steps.quote: Push the bolt all the way to the rear of the receiver, at the same time lift the front and release the bolt handle.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL RF-22LR — Radical Firearms — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Disassembly from the Receiver, step 8, p.7

steps.title: Bolt handle out through the ejection window
steps.action: Guide the bolt handle, with its recoil spring and guide rod, out through the ejection window. The spring is still on its guide; let the assembly come out under control rather than pulling it.
steps.quote: Guide the bolt handle out of the ejection window.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL RF-22LR — Radical Firearms — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Disassembly from the Receiver, step 9, p.7

steps.title: Bolt lifted out of the receiver
steps.action: Guide the bolt up and out of the receiver. It should come without force once the handle is gone.
steps.quote: Guide the bolt while lifting it out of the receiver.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL RF-22LR — Radical Firearms — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Disassembly from the Receiver, step 10, p.7

steps.title: Field strip complete — this is where Radical's book stops
steps.action: Stock, barreled receiver, trigger group, buffer pin, bolt handle assembly and bolt. Radical's disassembly ends here and points you at the cleaning; it publishes nothing past this point for the bolt or the trigger group.
steps.quote: At this point it is a good idea to thoroughly clean the receiver and barrel if needed.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL RF-22LR — Radical Firearms — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — Disassembly from the Receiver, step 11, p.7

deepAbsentReason: Radical's RF-22LR book ends its disassembly with the bolt lifted out of the receiver and a pointer to cleaning (p.7). It publishes no disassembly of the bolt, firing pin or trigger group — those parts appear only by name in the parts list (p.10). This listing therefore has NO deep clean.

cleaning.name: RECEIVER AND BARREL — after every use
tasks: Bolt out, receiver upside down, so the inside can be reached
Clear powder residue, unburned powder, bullet lube and lead from the receiver
Clean the barrel too, if it needs it — the book pairs it with the receiver
Tight tolerances: do this after each use, not when it starts to malfunction
cleaning.quote: Higher tolerances mean greater attention must be paid to regular lubrication and routine cleaning of your rifle after each use.
cleaning.src: INSTRUCTION MANUAL RF-22LR — Radical Firearms, General Information, Care and Maintenance, p.4

cleaning.name: RECOIL SPRING GUIDE CHANNEL — clean, then oil
tasks: Clean the channel the recoil spring guide rides in
Oil it lightly before the bolt handle goes back in
cleaning.quote: Turn receiver upside down, then clean and oil the recoil spring guide channel
cleaning.src: INSTRUCTION MANUAL RF-22LR — Radical Firearms, Assemble the RF22LR Enhanced Bolt Assembly into the Receiver, p.8

reassembly: Receiver upside down, recoil spring guide channel clean and oiled.
Bolt handle and recoil spring guide assembly in through the ejection port, so it nestles in the groove machined into the receiver.
Pull the bolt handle rearward and keep that pressure on the recoil spring while the groove on top of the bolt rests into the slot of the bolt handle.
Push down on the front of the bolt carefully until it seats onto the handle, then release slowly — the bolt and handle should now run smoothly.
Buffer pin back in at the rear of the receiver, trigger group in with its two side pins.
Barreled action back into the stock, takedown screw in, barrel band screw if the stock has one.
⛔ Never fire the rifle partly assembled — function check first.
fncheck: Magazine out, and look into the chamber to see it empty. Work the bolt by its handle several times: it should travel and return smoothly, which is the book's own test of a correctly seated bolt. Push the cross-bolt safety fully to ON and press the trigger — nothing should happen. ⛔ If the bolt drags or will not return, stop and take it back out: the bolt has not seated onto the handle, and the rifle must never be fired partly assembled.
